newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee seen ending 1997 lower - poll.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee seen ending 1997 lower - poll.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee, which has fallen just over three percent since the beginning of this year, is seen ending 1997 at 60.85 to the dollar, a Reuter poll of forex dealers showed on Monday.
The rupee was at 58.47 to the dollar at 0545 GMT on Monday.
It started the year at 56.70 to the dollar.

Eight leading foreign and local commercial banks in Sri Lanka said that the decline in the rupee's value will be in line with an annual depreciation of between five and eight percent as seen in the past few years.
Seylan Bank, however, said 60 rupees to the dollar was a more accurate value since it gave exporters a competitive advantage.
The banks said the Central Bank should not officially depreciate the rupee as it might prove harmful to the economy.
"A one-off depreciation of the rupee will be harmful to the current stability of the currency," said Hongkong Bank.
"Besides, the marginal advantages that could be gained by increased exports will be negated by high inflation due to cost of imports of essential commodities rising," it added.
In view of the country's heavy dependence on imports, a further depreciation of the rupee could have adverse socio-economic repercussions, Deutsche Bank said.
The state-owned Bank of Ceylon, however, said the rupee should be officially depreciated as speculation was not healthy.
The Central Bank fixes a daily dollar-rupee exchange rate range, based on the inflation differential between Sri Lanka and its major trading partners and local supply and demand.
It rarely intervenes in the market to support the rupee.
